On the upbeat side, the bull Narrative argued for a Fair Value of €14, assuming an 11.0% annual revenue growth rate and a shift from a loss of €2.4b to earnings of €12.5b by around 2028.

The bear Narrative put Fair Value at €6, based on a slower 3.5% yearly revenue growth rate and concern that reliance on internal combustion vehicles would keep pressure on margins.

Stellantis swung from a net loss of €4.5b in Q3 2025 to a smaller €535m loss in Q3 2026, with net margin improving from -12.2% to -1.4%. That supported the more optimistic view of a recovery in earnings power. However, profitability was still negative, which kept the cautious view on sustainable margins very much alive. Overall, the evidence pointed in both directions.

The key assumption was how quickly Stellantis could turn higher shipments and revenue into solid profits. For any automaker making big promises, it is important to check whether net margin actually moves decisively into positive territory and remains there before treating an earnings recovery story as established.
